summary: The unclassified group has 13 rows from two partitions: 12 symbolic links (11 in system_a, 1 in vendor_a) and one regular file, system/xbin/su. The links are absolute-path aliases to /data/cache, /system/bin, /system/etc, /storage/self/primary, /sys/kernel/debug, /odm/odm_dlkm/etc, /vendor/vendor_dlkm/etc, a shell bugreports directory under /data, and the /system_ext, /vendor, /product and /odm partition roots. plat_file_contexts labels these paths as rootfs, cache_file, vendor_file or system_file. The su file is a stripped AArch64 PIE ELF with interpreter /system/bin/linker64. It needs libc.so, libc++.so, libm.so and libdl.so, and the libc, libm and libdl names resolve through symlinks into the com.android.runtime APEX. Its usage text is "su [WHO [COMMAND...]]" with default shell /system/bin/sh, its mode bits are 4750 with owner 0:2000, and its file_contexts label is su_exec. The policy declares su and su_exec and contains a shell-to-su process transition. The system build.prop in the image reports Android release 12 and build type userdebug.

claims.claim: Embedded diagnostic and environment strings include: --help, setuid failed, setgid failed, invalid uid/gid '%s', setgroups failed, not allowed, too many group ids, failed to exec %s. Environment names read are PATH, USER and LOGNAME. The default shell path is /system/bin/sh, and a default PATH literal is embedded.
claims.label: verified
claims.evidence: strings -n 4 mnt/system_a/system/xbin/su | grep -nE '^--help|failed|invalid|not allowed|too many|^PATH|^USER|^LOGNAME|^/system/bin/sh|^/product/bin' -> 30:--help ; 31:setuid failed ; 32:setgid failed ; 33:invalid uid/gid '%s' ; 34:/system/bin/sh ; 35:setgroups failed ; 36:not allowed ; 37:too many group ids ; 38:PATH ; 39:USER ; 44:/product/bin:/apex/com.android.runtime/bin:/apex/com.android.art/bin:/system_ext/bin:/system/bin:/system/xbin:/odm/bin:/vendor/bin:/vendor/xbin ; 45:failed to exec %s ; 46:LOGNAME
claims.reason: All listed strings are present at the stated lines, and the default shell path (0x8ca) and default PATH literal (0x9d9) are embedded. The 'read' part is wrong. The binary imports setenv and unsetenv but no getenv. Disassembly shows PATH (0x911), USER (0x916) and LOGNAME (0xa7b) passed as the name argument to setenv with overwrite 1 (calls at 0x14d0, 0x1500, 0x1514), and the default PATH literal as its value. IFS (0x8d9) is passed to unsetenv (0x14dc), and LOGNAME and USER are passed to unsetenv at 0x1538 and 0x1544. So the names are set or cleared, not read. Gap: runtime behaviour was not run.
claims.corrected_claim: The binary embeds --help, setuid failed, setgid failed, invalid uid/gid '%s', setgroups failed, not allowed, too many group ids and failed to exec %s, plus the environment names PATH, USER, LOGNAME, IFS. The default shell path /system/bin/sh and a default PATH literal (/product/bin:/apex/com.android.runtime/bin:...:/vendor/xbin) are embedded. The binary passes PATH, USER and LOGNAME to setenv (PATH with the default literal as value), and clears IFS, USER and LOGNAME with unsetenv at separate call sites. It imports no getenv, so these names are set or cleared rather than read.

claims.claim: The 12 links are most likely static content of the partition images, created when the images were built, rather than links made by init at boot. This is inferred from the absence of any init statement that creates them and from the identical 2009-01-01 timestamps on all entries.
claims.label: inferred
claims.evidence: Basis: U26 (no init symlink statement creates a group link name) and U22 (stat mtime fields of the links show the same 2009-01-01 date across partitions); the build step that created them was not located.
claims.reason: stat shows mtime 2009-01-01 00:00:00 UTC for all 12 group links. A search across all .rc files under mnt finds 42 symlink statements, and none creates a group link name. The inferred basis holds. Gap: the build step that created the links was not located.

claims.claim: The su binary is a switch-user command. From its strings and imports it takes an optional WHO and COMMAND, sets the group and user IDs and the supplementary group list, and executes COMMAND or /system/bin/sh. The helper names suggest that one helper parses the WHO string into IDs and another extracts UID, GID and group list.
claims.label: inferred
claims.evidence: Basis: U09 (usage text), U10 (setuid failed, setgid failed, setgroups failed, failed to exec %s, /system/bin/sh), U06 (setuid, setgid, setgroups, execvp imports) and U11 (helper names pwtoid and extract_uidgids). Behaviour was not run.
claims.reason: The imports include setuid, setgid, setgroups, execvp, setenv and unsetenv. The strings include the usage text and /system/bin/sh, and the helper names are pwtoid and extract_uidgids, so the inferred label is right. Gaps: behaviour was not run, and control flow between the call sites was not traced. The role table row for su is labelled 'verified', but 'switch-user command' is an inference from the usage text; 'inferred' would fit better.

claims.claim: Each of the 12 links is a plain alias for its target path. Its role is limited to the target path verified in U20, U21 and the arrival of the target in other partitions; the naming-based purposes (cache, sdcard, dlkm etc, bugreports) are not confirmed by any consumer.
claims.label: inferred
claims.evidence: Basis: U20 and U21 (readlink targets) and U24 (labels). No program was run to confirm the purpose of each alias.
claims.reason: The inferred label holds, but 'not confirmed by any consumer' is contradicted by U25. Init scripts reference cache (/cache), sdcard (/sdcard), bin (/bin/rm), d (/d/mmc0) and system/vendor (/system/vendor/bin/cnss-daemon) through the link paths. The consumers of the bugreports and dlkm links were not found in the files checked. The bugreport service uses the full target path, not the link name.
claims.corrected_claim: Each of the 12 links is a plain alias for its target path. Its role is limited to the target path verified in U20 and U21 and the arrival of the target in other partitions. Init scripts reference cache, sdcard, bin, d and system/vendor through their link paths (see U25), so those purposes have observed path references. The purposes of the bugreports, dlkm, etc, product, system_ext and odm links have no consumer confirmed in the files checked.

gaps: The payload apex_payload.img inside com.android.runtime.apex was not unpacked. The contents of linker64, libc.so, libm.so and libdl.so, and their symbol versions, were not examined because they belong to another subsystem.

The su machine code was not disassembled: the available objdump reported "can't disassemble for architecture UNKNOWN!" for this AArch64 file. Control flow, the exact system calls and the run-time behaviour of su were not established, and su was not executed.
The embedded debug data holds five FUNC symbols only, with no DWARF or type information. Local functions, data objects and string-to-code cross-references are unresolved.

Extended attributes and SELinux labels on the symlink inodes and on the su inode were not read. The labels given here come from file_contexts patterns only, and the effective label of each path was not confirmed.

The runtime targets /data/cache, /data/user_de/0/com.android.shell/files/bugreports, /storage/self/primary and /sys/kernel/debug are outside the mounted set, so their existence and contents were not verified.

The vendor_dlkm/etc and odm_dlkm/etc targets are not present under the vendor_a or odm_a trees. Their resolution through the separate dlkm partitions is inferred from the partition names and was not verified against an fstab.
The device mount points for system_a, vendor_a, odm_a, product_a and system_ext_a were inferred from the link targets. The fstab or init mount entries were not read.

The compiled policy odm_a/etc/selinux/precompiled_sepolicy was checked only for the presence of the string su_exec. It was not decoded, and effective access rules for su and su_exec were not computed.
Only the policy statements that name su or su_exec were listed. The full rule set for the su domain and the su_exec type was not enumerated.
The build step or manifest that created the 12 links was not located, so the origin of the links is inferred only.
The mode and ownership values come from the extracted tree (stat on the mounted copy), not from the original image's inode metadata.
The roles given for the symlinks describe their targets. Their purposes (aliases, legacy paths, compatibility) are inferred from names and were not confirmed by a consumer of each link.
